note: Given a request, does the skill resolve Yandex Cloud identities and assemble the exact DataLens RLSv2 shape without exposing credentials? The offline Python suite mechanically covers parsing, normalization, resolution, conversion, CLI naming, and missing-yc errors; these assertions require human or model judgement.

evals.name: resolve-mixed-subjects
evals.prompt: On datalens.yandex.cloud, resolve alice@example.com, the group Analysts, service-account ID aje-service-1, *, and userid into the subject objects for an rls2 rule. Handle the work for me rather than giving generic documentation.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks yc safely, obtains or selects the organization, runs the bundled resolver, and returns subject objects whose authoritative subject_id and subject_type values follow the documented mapping.

assertions.text: Runs scripts/rls_tool.py resolve instead of inventing IDs or switching to an unrelated browser/API workflow.
Each resolved entry contains subject_id, subject_name, and subject_type; the group is normalized to @group:Analysts and the supplied service-account ID to @sa:aje-service-1 before resolution.
Does not fabricate user or group IDs when organization lookup access is unavailable.

evals.name: convert-legacy-config
evals.prompt: Convert this legacy DataLens RLS config to exact rls2 JSON: {"field_a": "'Naperville': @group:Analysts\n*: bob"}. The target is datalens.yandex.cloud.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the bundled convert mode and returns field_a as a list of value/all rules, each containing a nested subject object plus allowed_value and pattern_type.

assertions.text: Uses scripts/rls_tool.py convert with the legacy JSON supplied through a file or stdin.
Returns {field_guid: [rules]} where every rule has subject, allowed_value, and pattern_type; it does not invent a value-to-identities map.
Warns that the updated dataset must send rls2 without the legacy rls field.

evals.name: recover-auth-safely
evals.prompt: The yc session used for DataLens RLS resolution has expired. Check it and recover without exposing any OAuth or IAM token in the transcript.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks command availability and authentication with token output redirected away, then uses federated SSO or a service-account key path and retries the silent probe.

assertions.text: Uses yc iam create-token with both stdout and stderr redirected and relies only on the exit status.
Never runs yc config list, yc config get token, or an unredirected token command and never asks the user to paste a token.
Uses yc init --federation-id for SSO or yc config set service-account-key with a file path rather than recommending a plain OAuth token.

evals.name: permission-denied
evals.prompt: yc is authenticated, but organization-manager user list returns PermissionDenied while resolving DataLens RLS subjects. Continue the migration.
evals.expected_output: The agent distinguishes permissions from authentication, explains the organization-manager.viewer requirement on the target organization, and stops resolution until access is granted.

assertions.text: Requests organization-manager.viewer or a higher Organization Manager role on the target organization.
Does not treat PermissionDenied as an empty organization, guess IDs, or ship unresolved access rules.
Does not repeatedly reauthenticate when the valid identity simply lacks permission.

evals.name: unresolved-subjects
evals.prompt: While converting a legacy DataLens rls configuration, the resolver cannot find user ghost or group @group:Former Employees. Show the rls2 migration output and tell me whether it is safe to apply.
evals.expected_output: The convert output retains both failures as notfound subjects with !FAILED_ names, summarizes them, and instructs the user to correct and rerun rather than apply the configuration.

assertions.text: Unresolved subjects are emitted as subject_type notfound instead of being silently dropped.
The display name uses !FAILED_ and the unresolved group preserves its readable group spec in subject_id.
Advises fixing the names and rerunning before applying the migrated rls2 configuration.
